title: Finite affine free maps generating one module stalk
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $\Lambda$ a commutative ring, and $F$ a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. For $x\in X$, let $\bar x$ be the geometric point given by an algebraic closure of its residue field. Assume $F_{\bar x}$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] is finitely generated over $\Lambda$. For an etale object $W$, let $P_W$ be the sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] of $V\mapsto\Lambda^{(\operatorname{Hom}_X(V,W))}$. Set $I=\{(W,f):W\text{ affine etale over }X, f:P_W\to F\}$. There is a finite subset $S\subset I$ such that the stalk map of $\bigoplus_{(W,f)\in S}P_W\to F$, induced by the maps $f$, is surjective at $\bar x$. No finiteness of the ring, constructibility, or compactness of the scheme is assumed.

source.place: Tag 095N, lemma-category-constructible-modules, sentence using finite type of each geometric stalk; explicit free generator construction as in Modules on Sites Tag 03DI.

proof.text: Represent a stalk element by a section z on a pointed etale neighbourhood (V,v). In Lean use Point.toPresheafFiber_jointly_surjective after shrinking the universe of the filtered-colimit preservation instance for forget (ModuleCat Λ).

Choose an affine open Spec R→V through v(default). The geometric point factors through it by the universal property of an open immersion. Restrict z along this open immersion and use Point.toPresheafFiber_w to keep the same germ.

For the resulting affine object W and section z, explicitly define a presheaf map η sending the generator indexed by h:V→W to F(h)(z). ModuleCat.freeDesc gives its linear components and functoriality proves naturality. Sheafify this map with sheafifyLift; toSheafify_sheafifyLift proves that the generator indexed by id_W maps to z. Point.toPresheafFiber_naturality therefore puts the chosen germ in the range of the stalk of the sheaf map.

Unpack Module.Finite.fg_top into a finite set T spanning the stalk. Choose one affine free map for each t∈T and take the finite image S of these choices. Each chosen map factors through the S-indexed coproduct injection. Applying the stalk functor and Sigma.ι_desc shows T is contained in the range of the total stalk map. The range is a submodule; Submodule.span_le and span(T)=top give range=top, hence surjectivity. Empty T produces empty S.
